evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days
The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS).

criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, four numbered objectives/requirements, and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) with needs explicitly mapped to objectives. Rationale is well referenced. Minor: [6] is a NOAA page cited for BoM SST products, and [4] is a news article rather than the primary method paper.

evidence.quote: The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time
Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it.

criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with completed/planned coding and deadlines, per-task descriptions, a risk/contingency table with triggers and responses, and a sources table. Plan is explicitly justified against the mission sequence (orbit before comms, EOL after orbit). Robust and feasible.

evidence.quote: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes
A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.

criteria.reasoning: Hand calculations for a, T, orbits/day, SSO inclination, ground-track shift and swath are all numerically correct (T=5801 s, 14.9 rev/day, 24.2 deg, 60 km). Interpretation identifies the swath/coverage trade and links it to a contingency. STK work is only just started, so progress is good but early.

evidence.quote: Table 2 lists the sources I plan to use and what each is for.
[7] J. R. Wertz, D. F. Everett, and J. J. Puschell, Eds., Space Mission Engineering: The New SMAD.

criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear headings, professional prose, consistent formatting. Figure 1 and Tables 1-3 are labelled and captioned. All eleven references are cited in text and appear in the list in a consistent style. Only minor citation-content mismatches.

technical_issues.issue: Reference [6] (NOAA climate-change page) is cited as the source for the Bureau of Meteorology combining imagery with SST products; citation does not support the claim.
Objective 2 is to be refined against [4], but [4] is a Nature news article, not the primary Asner method paper; the 10 m GSD requirement is therefore not traceable to a technical source.
'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' is a simplification; the underlying change is a ~0.1 pH-unit drop (~30% rise in H+ concentration).
The 97.8 deg sun-synchronous inclination is stated without showing the J2 nodal-precession calculation, so the key result is unverifiable from the report.
The 60 km swath assumes 6,000 cross-track pixels but no detector/pixel-size justification is given, and the 250 km reef width is not referenced.

overall: Strong, well-structured preliminary report. Mission concept, users and requirements are clear and referenced; the Gantt chart, contingencies and source table form a credible plan; hand calculations are correct and interpreted. Main gaps are a few citation-content mismatches and limited STK work to date.
